checks.finding: terms-contradict-mapping: usage: inverse vs terms inverse+surface (terms: on-surface, inverse, on, surface)
terms-contradict-mapping: usage: inverse vs terms inverse+surface (terms: inverse, surface)
terms-contradict-mapping: usage: (unbound) vs terms surface (terms: on-surface, on, surface, variant)
terms-contradict-mapping: property: (unbound) vs terms background (terms: scrim)

evidence.says: background: A color that typically appears behind scrollable content.
Identical values in both themes; surface is mapped narrow because it also serves as the page background. background is the page-only role.
The M3 roles page no longer lists background as a role; surface is 'Default color for backgrounds'.

verdicts.note: Legacy role retained by material-web; page background is the only documented meaning.

evidence.says: Error: Attention-grabbing color against surface for fills, icons, and text, indicating urgency
58 uses across text (30), icon (8), border (6) and badge fills: no single property, so bare intent is right.

verdicts.note: narrow matches color-v1.md: error also colors destructive and badge fills beyond danger status.

evidence.says: Error container: Attention-grabbing fill color against surface
error90 light / error30 dark: a light tonal fill, lower emphasis than error (error40/error80).
Inverse on surface: Text and icons against inverse surface
Icon (4) and state-layer (2) roles on the inverse-surface selected container: foreground.

verdicts.note: The terms check flags 'surface', but the docs place the role on inverse surface; usage-inverse/property-foreground is the right reading.

evidence.says: Inverse primary: Actionable elements, such as text buttons, against inverse surface
primary80 light / primary40 dark: the primary tone swapped across themes.
Inverse surface: Background fills for elements which contrast against surface
Used as a container (background) color.
onBackground: A color that's clearly legible when drawn on background.
Identical values; on-surface -> usage-surface/property-foreground (exact), so the page counterpart is usage-page/property-foreground.
On error: Text and icons against error
Label text on the error-filled badge.
Content on a filled background -> usage-on-fill + property, exact; on-error is the listed example.
On error container: Text and icons against error container
Text (6), icon (4), border (3): foreground on the light error container.
emphasis-subtle for light containers; on-error-container is the listed example.
On primary: Text and icons against primary
Icon (16) and text (5) on primary-filled components.
On primary container: Text and icons against primary container
Icon (8) and text (4) on the primary-container FAB.
On fixed colors are used for text and icons which sit on top of the corresponding Fixed color; Primary fixed ... are fill colors used against surface.
primaryFixed: A substitute for primaryContainer that's the same color for the dark and light themes.
primary10 #21005d in both themes = on-primary-container light (primary10), not on-primary (primary100 #ffffff).

verdicts.note: The fixed convention is right but the counterpart is on-primary-container, not on-primary; the mapping drops emphasis-subtle.

evidence.says: Secondary: Less prominent fills, text, and icons against surface; on-<role> is text and icons against that role.
Secondary and tertiary accent roles -> intent-accent, broad.
Secondary container: Less prominent fill color against surface, for recessive components like tonal buttons
Icon (40) and text (25) on secondary-container fills.
On fixed colors are used for text and icons which sit on top of the corresponding Fixed color; fixed roles are fill colors used against surface.
secondary10 #1d192b in both themes = on-secondary-container light, not on-secondary (secondary100 #ffffff).

verdicts.note: Counterpart is on-secondary-container (broad per the secondary convention), so emphasis-subtle belongs.

evidence.says: On surface: Text and icons against any surface or surface container color
236 uses, text (88) and icon (49) dominate; one token for text and icons -> property-foreground.
On surface variant: Lower-emphasis color for text and icons against any surface or surface container color
Text (50) and icon (62) in supporting roles: subtle foreground.

verdicts.note: Docs place it on surfaces exactly like on-surface; dsi:concept/color/usage-surface/property-foreground/emphasis-subtle exists and would be the tighter concept. Not wrong, only less specific.

evidence.says: Tertiary: Complementary fills, text, and icons against surface; on-<role> is text and icons against that role.
Secondary and tertiary accent roles -> intent-accent, broad.
Tertiary container: Complementary container color against surface, for components like input fields
Icon (4) and text (4) on the tertiary-container FAB.
On fixed colors are used for text and icons which sit on top of the corresponding Fixed color; fixed roles are fill colors used against surface.
tertiary10 #31111d in both themes = on-tertiary-container light, not on-tertiary (tertiary100 #ffffff).

verdicts.note: Counterpart is on-tertiary-container, so emphasis-subtle belongs.

evidence.says: Outline: Important boundaries, such as a text field outline
15 of 16 uses are border roles.
Outline variant: Decorative elements, such as dividers, and when other elements provide 4.5:1 contrast
Divider and card outline: low-emphasis borders.
Primary: High-emphasis fills, texts, and icons against surface
148 uses across icon, text, background, border: the brand accent with no single property.
Primary container: Standout fill color against surface, for key components like FAB
primaryContainer: A color used for elements needing less emphasis than primary.
Container (background) fill.

verdicts.note: close is apt: a tonal accent fill, lower emphasis than primary but still a standout fill.

evidence.says: Primary fixed ... are fill colors used against surface.
primaryFixed: A substitute for primaryContainer that's the same color for the dark and light themes.
primary90 #eaddff in both themes = primary-container light, not primary (primary40 #6750a4).

verdicts.note: Fixed convention applies, but the counterpart is primary-container (a fill), not primary; exact to bare intent-accent overstates a light tonal fill.

evidence.says: scrim: A color use to paint the scrim around of modal components.
Named as a role in the 'Scrim and Shadow roles' figure.

verdicts.note: The property check wants background; usage-scrim already names the modal backdrop, so leaving property unbound is fine.

evidence.says: Secondary: Less prominent fills, text, and icons against surface
Secondary and tertiary accent roles -> intent-accent, broad.
Secondary container: Less prominent fill color against surface, for recessive components like tonal buttons
9 of 11 uses are container (background) fills.
Fixed roles are fill colors used against surface, the same tone in light and dark themes.
secondary90 #e8def8 in both themes = secondary-container light, not secondary (secondary40 #625b71).

verdicts.note: Counterpart is secondary-container, which maps to the accent subtle background, broad.

evidence.says: shadow: A color use to paint the drop shadows of elevated components.
All 14 uses are *-shadow-color tokens.
Surface: Default color for backgrounds
7 of 9 uses are container backgrounds.
Identical values; surface also serves as the page background, so it covers more than usage-surface: narrow.
Surface bright: Brightest surface color in light and dark themes
neutral98 light / neutral24 dark: one specific surface level -> broad.
Surface container: Default container color
All 3 uses are container backgrounds.

verdicts.note: Middle level of the ordered family; dsi:concept/color/usage-surface/property-background/emphasis-default exists and would let it sit beside the low/high siblings with close.

evidence.says: Surface container high: High-emphasis container color
All 3 uses are container backgrounds.
Surface container highest: Highest-emphasis container color
Container backgrounds (6); icon uses are disabled-state tints.
Surface container low: Low-emphasis container color
All 8 uses are container backgrounds.
Surface container lowest: Lowest-emphasis container color
neutral100 light / neutral4 dark: the end of the 5-step family -> subtlest.
Surface dim: Dimmest surface color in light and dark themes
neutral87 light / neutral6 dark: one specific surface level -> broad.
surfaceVariant: A color variant of surface that can be used for differentiation against a component using surface.
No longer listed as a role on the M3 roles page (superseded by surface container levels).

verdicts.note: Legacy role still shipped by material-web; one surface variant -> broad.

evidence.says: Tertiary: Complementary fills, text, and icons against surface
Secondary and tertiary accent roles -> intent-accent, broad.
Tertiary container: Complementary container color against surface, for components like input fields
Container (background) fill.
Fixed roles are fill colors used against surface, the same tone in light and dark themes.
tertiary90 #ffd8e4 in both themes = tertiary-container light, not tertiary (tertiary40 #7d5260).

verdicts.note: Counterpart is tertiary-container, which maps to the accent subtle background, broad.
